newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble stable sustained by T-bill, OFZ bond sales.
newsitem.headline: Rouble stable sustained by T-bill, OFZ bond sales.

text.p: The rouble was little changed in lively trading on Wednesday but overnight credit rates rose as commercial banks closed positions after setting aside funds for today's government bond sales, dealers said.
"Money seems to have been sent to the auctions and banks need to sell dollars to close their positions," one dealer said, adding credit rates could ease later today.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 70-80 percent compared with Tuesday's late 40-60 percent.
Today the central bank is auctioning 7.50 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills and sold 3.50 trillion roubles of an additional tranche of OFZ interest-bearing bonds.
Some dealers said the rouble's relative stability, seen all this week, could herald the start of an upward trend.
"The dollar was rising notably in August and its selling could start now. On the other hand, dollar rates are not falling much," one dealer said.
Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,367-70 per dollar compared with an early 5,373-76 and 5,373-75 late on Tuesday. Tomorrow roubles were steady at the 5,375-78 per dollar level.
The central bank said it had set 5,344/5,384 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Wednesday.
